summary: Reviewed all 4 modified files: project-meta.ts, root-index.ts, ledger-store.ts, and tests/schema/project-meta.test.ts.
No blocking issues found. Implementation is minimal, correct, and strictly backward-compatible.

The outcome_summary field follows the established z.string().nullable().optional() convention already used by project_name and repository_name in ProjectMetaSchema — consistent placement and identical Zod shape.

writeProjectMeta() correctly uses the 'in cacheUpdates' guard for outcome_summary (same as project_name/repository_name), distinguishing nullable overrides (must use key-presence check) from non-nullable ones (undefined check is sufficient).

Test file is well-structured: shared BASE_META / BASE_ROOT fixtures reduce boilerplate, tests cover all three valid states (string, null, absent) and three invalid types (number, boolean, object). AC references in test names are a nice traceability touch.
One documentation-forward observation raised for the Documentation agent — the parameter JSDoc on writeProjectMeta() does not mention outcome_summary as a supported cacheUpdates key.

comments.note: The two-phase spread pattern in writeProjectMeta() (preserve-existing then cacheUpdates-override) is correct and consistent across all nullable fields. A future refactor could consolidate the repeated ternary spreads into a typed helper (e.g., spreadIfPresent / spreadIfInUpdates) to reduce boilerplate, but this is cosmetic — the current approach is clear and safe.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc comment on writeProjectMeta() (ledger-store.ts ~line 467) describes the @param cacheUpdates as 'Optional WP counter / enrichment fields' but does not enumerate the supported keys. Now that outcome_summary is a first-class cache field, the JSDoc should list it alongside project_name and repository_name so maintainers know the full surface without reading the MetaCacheUpdates interface separately.
